workflows.name: Architecture Review Board & Solution Architecture Review

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "prepare the solution-architecture artifact for the initiative" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-review of "review the solution architecture" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-track of "track conformance to the approved architecture through delivery" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-568 (ensure controlled execution — Enterprise Architecture Framework, Standards & Governance (PA-113.1).)
- operational: clear criteria and quorum; operational: tiered review (light for minor, full for major) and cadence
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rubber-stamp risk**: ARB approves without rigor; mitigated by clear criteria and quorum
- **Bottleneck risk**: ARB backlog stalls projects; mitigated by tiered review (light for minor, full for major) and cadence
System Touchpoints: - PMIS/intake (links to VS-112/W3546); repository (links to W3575); standards (links to W3572); security (links to VS-27.3); operations (links to VS-27.1); data (links to VS-28.2)

ARB review the solution architecture: principle/standard conformance (W3570/W3572), reuse vs. build/buy, integration approach (W3579), data implications (W3581), security posture (W3583), operational readiness (links to VS-27.1), and total cost (links to W3588); decision — approve, approve-with-conditions, revise, or reject; capture conditions and waivers (W3573)

workflows.name: SEP Paved Road & Engineering Standard Governance for Built Products

Automation Opportunity: - Golden-path bootstrap auto-provisions repo, CI/CD, observability and IaC from the service template (replaces manual Step 1 assembly).
- DORA metrics auto-aggregated from pipeline and incident telemetry (replaces manual Step 5 collation).
Controls: - CTL-568 (ensure controlled execution — Enterprise Architecture Framework, Standards & Governance (PA-113.1).)
- operational: 100% golden-path starts — deviations only via ARB-recorded exception (W3573)
- operational: security gates — SAST + dependency scan per merge, DAST before ring expansion, SBOM per release; AppSec block right
- operational: production readiness review (SEP + INFRA) before first fleet ring
Pain Points / Risks: - **Paved-road-drift risk**: squads assemble private toolchains that fragment delivery and security posture; mitigated by golden-path templates, the ARB-exception record, and QBR adoption reporting (100% minus exceptions)

- **Fleet-first risk**: a change reaches the fleet without canary evidence or security gates; mitigated by automated SLO-burn rollback gates, the AppSec block right on ring expansion, and the production-readiness review as a launch criterion
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed within the sized SEP platform team (Head of Engineering + DevEx ×2 + AppSec + QA-automation lead + designer + build SRE, OM §5.3/§9.1); the standard is enforced by the paved road, not added headcount.
System Touchpoints: - SEP golden-path service templates (repo layout, CI/CD, observability, IaC provisioning)
- Ring-deployment infrastructure (internal → canary → fleet) with automated SLO-burn rollback gates
- AppSec gate suite — SAST, dependency scan, DAST, SBOM, secrets scanning
- Contract-testing harness against IAP-published contracts (links to W3579)
- DORA dashboards & the ARB exception register (links to W3573)
Time Estimate: Production readiness reviews ~8–16 hours/service × ~12–24 first-fleet services/year ≈ 96–384 hours/year; exception reviews ~2–4 hours/exception × ~6–12 exceptions/year ≈ 12–48 hours/year; quarterly DORA/adoption reporting ~4–6 hours/quarter × 4 quarters ≈ 16–24 hours/year. Total **≈ 124–456 hours/year** (≈0.06–0.22 FTE), absorbed within the sized SEP team.

steps.activity: DevEx bootstrap every new service from the SEP golden-path templates — repo layout, CI/CD, observability, IaC; any deviation requires an ARB-recorded exception (W3573), and paved-road adoption (100% minus recorded exceptions) is reported at QBR

SEP enforce the engineering standard: trunk-based development with feature flags (no long-lived branches); contract-first integration — every cross-product call is an IAP-published contract with consumer-driven contract tests, no direct database access (links to W3579); data contracts on every DP-published dataset

Squads deploy on the ring model — internal ring → canary stores/DCs → fleet — with automated SLO-burn rollback gates, independent of the ERP monthly train; the AppSec engineer runs the security gates: SAST + dependency scan on every merge, DAST before each ring expansion, SBOM per release, secrets never in code — and can block a ring expansion
SEP + INFRA run the production readiness review before the first fleet ring: on-call runbook, SLOs, capacity model, DR posture — typhoon-season resilience is a launch criterion, not a follow-up

Head of Engineering report squad DORA targets at QBR — deployment frequency ≥ weekly, change lead time < 1 week, MTTR < 4 hours, change-failure rate < 15% — alongside product outcome KPIs; changes touching Tier-1 workflows carry Tier & Control Board sign-off (links to W1409/W391)
